title: Where can I find care information for an individual piece?
description: Start with the care information supplied for the actual piece and its confirmed material and finish.

sections.heading: Where can I find care information for an individual piece?
paragraphs: Start with the care information supplied for the actual piece and its confirmed material and finish. Use the materials and care page for general context, then ask the atelier about anything unclear. A similar-looking product or editorial image does not establish interchangeable care instructions. Include the piece or inquiry reference in the question.

title: Should care questions mention the confirmed material and finish?

sections.heading: Should care questions mention the confirmed material and finish?
paragraphs: Yes. Include the confirmed material and finish where known, the piece reference and the actual use or concern. If those details are unknown, say so rather than identifying them from appearance. Photographs can explain context but cannot certify composition. Ask for guidance tied to the actual piece before choosing a cleaning or treatment method.

title: Can an image establish heat resistance?

sections.heading: Can an image establish heat resistance?
paragraphs: No. A photograph, visualization or prop does not establish heat resistance or a temperature limit. Describe the intended use and ask for guidance based on the actual confirmed material and finish. Do not test heat exposure because a reference scene contains a candle, cup or other warm-looking object. Appearance is not performance evidence.

title: Can I infer food-contact suitability from a product photograph?

sections.heading: Can I infer food-contact suitability from a product photograph?
paragraphs: No. A product name, plate-like shape or photograph containing food does not establish food-contact suitability for a proposed piece. Ask about the actual material, finish and intended use before making that assumption. A decorative illustration communicates appearance; it cannot replace the appropriate specification or supporting information for a suitability claim.

title: Where should cleaning questions be directed?
description: Ask the atelier with the piece reference, confirmed specification and the specific cleaning question.

sections.heading: Where should cleaning questions be directed?
paragraphs: Ask the atelier with the piece reference, confirmed specification and the specific cleaning question. Include relevant photographs if they help explain a concern. Do not choose chemicals, abrasives or repair methods from an inspiration image or a general article. Follow the instructions for the actual piece and request clarification when their scope is unclear.

title: What placement conditions should I describe?
description: Describe nearby windows, heat sources, moisture, frequent contact and normal use where relevant.

sections.heading: What placement conditions should I describe?
paragraphs: Describe nearby windows, heat sources, moisture, frequent contact and normal use where relevant. Note any recent move or change in conditions. Keep observations separate from a diagnosis of what caused a concern. These details support a piece-specific discussion; they do not establish technical exposure values or prove that the material is suitable for the location.

title: How do I photograph a surface concern?
description: Take a whole-piece view and a closer view of the area in useful light, without filters where possible.

sections.heading: How do I photograph a surface concern?
paragraphs: Take a whole-piece view and a closer view of the area in useful light, without filters where possible. Record when it was noticed and relevant changes in use or placement. Describe what is visible rather than assigning a cause. Include the inquiry reference and consult the current concern-reporting policy before attempting repairs.

title: Does general guidance replace piece-specific instructions?

sections.heading: Does general guidance replace piece-specific instructions?
paragraphs: No. General guidance provides context but does not replace instructions for the actual confirmed material, finish and use. Keep piece-specific notes with the current specification and ask about any apparent conflict. Do not strengthen a broad suggestion into a warranty, certification or performance limit, or borrow instructions from an unrelated similar-looking object.

title: Can I discuss relocation before moving a piece?
description: Discuss the proposed move before assuming the original handling or installation arrangement applies.

sections.heading: Can I discuss relocation before moving a piece?
paragraphs: Discuss the proposed move before assuming the original handling or installation arrangement applies. Describe the current and new positions, route, turns, stairs or lifts, and the piece's confirmed dimensions. Ask what assessment is needed. This is not a moving instruction, and the website does not promise installation at every destination.

title: Where can I ask about a care instruction I do not understand?
description: Contact the atelier with the piece reference, the instruction you are trying to understand and the action you are considering.

sections.heading: Where can I ask about a care instruction I do not understand?
paragraphs: Contact the atelier with the piece reference, the instruction you are trying to understand and the action you are considering. Include the confirmed material and finish if available. Asking a specific question is safer than guessing from a general article or photograph. Keep any clarification with the care record for that piece.
